declared: 2026-10-23, before any BF16-derived candidate was built or scored
question: Do NVFP4 expert weights quantized from the original BF16 checkpoints, with a per-expert F32 scale, pass the unchanged precision gates that the requantized candidates failed?

sources.integrity: All 195 safetensors files matched their pinned Git LFS SHA-256 before use.

selection: Same expert tensors as the requantized screens (Nemotron 80 ffn_up/down_exps in layers 0-87, MTP layer excluded; Flash-Next 144 ffn_gate/up/down_exps in layers 0-47). Every other tensor payload and all metadata except split.tensors.count stay byte-identical to the original GGUF.

encoder.name: scaled per-expert NVFP4
encoder.per_expert_scale: s_e = amax(|W_e|) / (6 * 240), stored as blk.N.ffn_X_exps.scale (F32, n_expert), the existing optional loader tensor
encoder.weights: ggml_quantize_chunk(GGML_TYPE_NVFP4) of W_e / s_e from the installed ggml-base.dll; no imatrix
encoder.cap_reason: ggml_fp32_to_ue4m3 maps every block scale of 256 or more to 448, so 240 is the largest exact UE4M3 block scale
encoder.alternative_not_run: Plain unscaled NVFP4 from BF16 was considered and not selected; only its per-expert reconstruction error is reported as a diagnostic.

mapping_check: Before a build, sampled experts must match the original GGUF experts in shape, and their BF16 values must correlate with the dequantized original tensors at Pearson r >= 0.95.
gates: Unchanged from the parent: actual-PPL ratio <= 1.01 and mean KL <= 0.01 against the same-model calibration, calibration |KL| <= 0.001 and actual PPL within 0.01%, same corpus, chunks, context, batch and runtime.
stop: A failed model is documented and not enabled. No subset narrowing, scale-cap sweep, activation-precision change or threshold relaxation. A pass only allows held-out quality and speed validation; it enables nothing.
